title: Operational Audit Indexing and Residency Playbook
author: Lena Ortega
content:
Overview This playbook defines operational patterns for indexing audit events, mapping audit storage to geographic residency and retention policies, and integrating RBAC/authorization signals with compliance evidence workflows. It is intended for SRE, security, and infra teams who operate the audit pipeline, and for engineering teams that must produce forensic-quality evidence during incidents. Objectives - Ensure audit events are indexed and queryable within SLOs required by compliance and incident response. - Attach authoritative residency and retention metadata to each audit event. - Provide deterministic evidence collection runbooks for incidents that preserve chain-of-custody. - Integrate secure-SDLC gates so releases cannot remove required audit telemetry. Scope - Applies to: service-to-service auth logs, user-level authorization events (grant/revoke/role-change), model-serving inference audit events, admin console actions, and orchestration job logs. - Excludes: ephemeral debug logs written to developer laptops or external third-party SaaS logs (those must be ingested via connectors described below). Definitions - Event TTL: configured retention period for a given event type (see Retention Matrix). - Residency Tag: a canonical tag on each event indicating the legal region of custody (e.g., eu, us, apac). - Evidence Bundle: a time-bounded collection of events and artifacts used for a compliance request or forensic analysis. Ownership and Roles - Audit Pipeline Owner: eng-platform/audit-team (primary) — responsible for ingestion, indexing, and retention enforcement. - Evidence Custodian: security-ops — owns packaging and legal handoff for Evidence Bundles. - Service Owners: individual service teams — ensure their services emit the canonical audit schema and residency metadata. - SRE Oncall: operational response and temporary retention extension during incidents. Indexing and Storage Patterns 1) Canonical Schema (required fields) - event_id (UUID v4) - timestamp_utc (ISO8601) - service (string) - event_type (enum: auth, authz, admin, data_access, model_inference, infra) - principal_id (string) - principal_type (enum: user, service_account, system) - action (string) - resource (string) - outcome (enum: success, failure, unknown) - residency (enum: us, eu, apac, other) - retention_policy_id (string) - trace_id (optional) - tx_payload_hash (optional sha256) 2) Indexing requirements - Primary index on (timestamp_utc, service). Secondary indexes on (event_type), (principal_id), and (residency). - Events must be available for query at 1s latency for last-24h and 30s for last-7d under normal load. These are operational SLOs. 3) Partitioning and hot-paths - Partition by residency/residency_region + service + date (UTC date). This simplifies geo-fenced exports and legal holds. - Hot-path telemetry (admin console, role-change events) should be forwarded to the immutable cold-storage write-ahead log in parallel to the searchable index. Retention and Residency Policy Matrix | retention_policy_id | event_types | default_ttl | residency_affinity | legal_hold_extension | |---------------------|------------------------------------------|-------------|--------------------|----------------------| | RP-90D | admin, authz, auth (successful/failed) | 90 days | us, eu, apac | +180 days | | RP-2Y | data_access (sensitive), model_explain | 2 years | per-resource | +2 years (audit req) | | RP-7Y | privileged_key_rotation, entitlement_audits | 7 years | per-contract | +7 years | | RP-30D | infra, telemetry (non-sensitive) | 30 days | global | +90 days | - Residency_affinity: default mapping from tenant or resource to residency. Service owners must ensure residency tag is set at emission time (see Emission checklist). Compliance Evidence Workflow (operational steps) 1) Evidence request intake - Security receives request (internal IR, legal subpoena, regulatory). Create a ticket in Evidence-Tracker (prefix EVID-). - Record scope (service list, time window, tenant IDs) and required residency rules. 2) Scoped collection - Audit Pipeline Owner runs a scoped export job: export-events --service --start --end --residency --policy RP-* - Mark export snapshot id and store in Evidence Locker (immutable object store path: s3://evidence-locker//snapshots//). 3) Evidence packaging and integrity - Package events with schema-version metadata, compression (gzip), and SHA256 manifest. Example manifest: { "snapshot_id": "snap-20240510-01", "schema_version": "v1.3", "sha256": "" } - Evidence Custodian attaches an audit trail: who exported, which queries were run, and retention hold flags. 4) Chain-of-custody and legal handoff - All packaging operations must be logged to the immutable WORM ledger and an export notification dispatched to security/legal. - If the request crosses residency boundaries, perform a residency proof of export: include export logs showing the location of the source partitions and the export target. Secure-SDLC Integration - Release gates: the CI/CD pipeline must run an audit-coverage check on pull requests touching services emitting audit events. The check ensures: - schema-version bump included if audit fields changed, - unit/integration tests generate sample audit events captured by the local test-index, and - a migration plan exists for index schema changes. - Example CI step (bash): - run: scripts/ci/audit_schema_check.sh --service $SERVICE --schema-file ./schemas/audit.json Incident Response Hooks - Short-term retention extension (legal hold) 1. SRE oncall or security-ops may request a temporary retention extension up to 90 days for partitions matching an incident ticket. Use CLI: retentionctl extend --policy RP-30D --partition

--days 90 --ticket . 2. Extensions must be approved by Evidence Custodian within 24 hours; approval is recorded in Evidence-Tracker. - Emergency export (for active incident) - Use stream-snap to create a consistent snapshot: stream-snap --trace --window 5m --output /tmp/.jsonl - Immediately copy to evidence-locker and notify security-ops channel (#sec-ops-evidence). Risk and Exceptions Handling - Risk types: missing residency tags, schema drift, retention enforcement failures, evidence leakage. - Exception workflow: 1. Service owner files an Authorization Exception (AE-) when a required control cannot be met. 2. Risk Review Board (sec+legal+platform) evaluates and records compensating controls and an exception TTL (max 90 days without re-approval). 3. Evidence Custodian schedules an audit to validate compensating controls at exception expiry. Monitoring and SLOs - Pipeline indexing availability: 99.9% (monthly). - Query latency: 95th pct under normal load: last-24h < 1s, last-7d < 30s. - Snapshot integrity: 100% of exported snapshots must have valid SHA256 and schema_version tag. Failures create a high-priority issue and notify the oncall. Emitters: Developer Checklist (before merging changes) - [ ] Add residency metadata to emitted events. - [ ] Reference a retention_policy_id. - [ ] Add integration tests that assert indexability. - [ ] Include a short migration plan for schema changes. Operational Commands and Examples - Query example (Kusto-like): events | where service == "auth-service" and timestamp_utc between(datetime(2024-05-01) .. datetime(2024-05-02)) | where event_type == "authz" | project timestamp_utc, principal_id, action, outcome, residency - Export example (CLI): audit-export --ticket EVID-1234 --service auth-service --start 2024-05-01T00:00:00Z --end 2024-05-02T00:00:00Z --residency eu --out s3://evidence-locker/EVID-1234/snap-01.jsonl.gz Appendices A. Example audit event (JSON) { "event_id": "1c3f2a7a-6d4c-4b05-9fb2-0a1d2e3f4b5c", "timestamp_utc": "2024-05-01T12:34:56.789Z", "service": "auth-service", "event_type": "authz", "principal_id": "user|U12345", "principal_type": "user", "action": "role.grant", "resource": "project:proj-99", "outcome": "success", "residency": "eu", "retention_policy_id": "RP-90D", "trace_id": "trace-xyz-0001" } B. Evidence packaging checklist - Confirm schema_version and sha256 manifest. - Document query used to produce snapshot and the exporter principal id. - Lock snapshot into Evidence Locker with immutable flag. C. FAQ Q: Who can request a legal hold? A: Security-ops or Legal only. Engineering may request an incident-based temporary extension through SRE oncall. Q: What happens if retention enforcement deletes evidence needed for a live investigation? A: File an emergency recovery ticket; the Evidence Custodian will coordinate restoration from cold backups if available and escalate to Legal. Related documents - Schema versioning playbook (see related_pages) - Authorization logging best practices (see related_pages) Change log - 2024-03-15: Created by Lena Ortega. - 2024-11-02: Added retention CLI patterns and Evidence Locker path. - 2025-05-10: Revised SLO targets and added partitioning guidance for residency-based exports.
